text:
leo_ae: Ping — ClearTrust (payments) asked for a private POC. Requirements: no public ingress into their VPC, outbound traffic must be allowlisted to a short set of static IPs, and their IDS/forensics team needs original client IPs on logs. They want guidance on PrivateLink vs TGW/Peering, a practical egress pattern, exact firewall lines to hand to their netops, and a very rough cost delta vs Dedicated for initial sizing.

rachel_se: quick Qs before the presales: single account? are they doing cross-account SaaS integrations? expected RPS & burst? any mutual-TLS or cert requirements?

leo_ae: single AWS account today. Steady ~120 rps, burst ~600. They do PCI scope and require KMS + CloudTrail retention. No mTLS required initially but they may request it for control-plane APIs.

omar_arch: short take: PrivateLink (NLB + VPCE) is recommended if they insist on "no public ingress" and want minimal changes to route tables. TGW/peering gives L3 access and lower latency (useful for heavier internal integrations), but demands CIDR planning and a longer security review.

omar_arch: practical egress patterns we use:
- Pattern A (recommended): Customer-managed egress proxy in their VPC with a static EIP. We send traffic to that proxy over PrivateLink. Proxy forwards outbound so customer controls EIP and can preserve headers (X-Forwarded-For).
- Pattern B: Deploy small agent/private node in customer subnets (we can run it in their account). Egress from their NAT Gateway with static EIPs; NAT will SNAT so original source IP is not preserved unless they route return traffic back to preserve it.
- Pattern C: Full TGW/peering with route exchange — good for many integrations but more operational overhead.

julie_netops: firewall snippet to paste into their security questionnaire (copy/paste):

```
# ClearTrust firewall egress snippet for Redwood POC
- Protocol: TCP
- Ports: 443
- Destination: <VPCE CIDR e.g. 10.200.50.0/27> OR <Redwood EIP set: 203.0.113.10, 203.0.113.11>
- Description: Redwood Inference private endpoints / egress
# Optional: allow TCP 8000 from Redwood ops/control-plane IPs for agent healthchecks (confirm exact list with ops)
```

rachel_se: TLS inspection note: if ClearTrust does TLS interception, request SNI allowlisting for our hostnames or opt for passthrough via VPCE+NLB. If they want mutual TLS for control-plane calls, we need cert exchange ahead of the POC.

leo_ae: source-IP preservation — they insist on raw client IPs visible on-prem. Which pattern actually achieves that?

julie_netops: two real options:
1) Customer egress proxy: they terminate from our side and forward preserving headers; logs show client IP in X-Forwarded-For. This is simple and keeps control with them.
2) If they need L2/L3 preservation to on-prem (no header trick), they must accept asymmetric routing and advertise return routes (complex). Not recommended for POC.

omar_arch: cost delta (very rough for scoping):
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool): predictable monthly commit. Example: 1x8-GPU pool ballpark ~$18k-$22k/month depending on model and batching.
- Private (customer-managed infra): Redwood platform/setup fee (one-time) ~$25k-$40k, annual support ~$8k-$15k, plus infra costs billed in their AWS account (EC2/GPU/NAT/EIPs). Exact quote requires finance.

rachel_se: blockers to flag in presales: CIDR overlap (for peering/TGW), strict no-external-IP policies (if they reject any EIP we need PrivateLink+customer proxy), requirements for an airgapped admin/control plane, and KMS/HSM expectations.

saas-bot: reminder: create tech-handoff invite and upload security questionnaire to the shared drive.

leo_ae: next steps: scheduling 30m tech handoff with ClearTrust + their netops for tomorrow 9am PT. @omar_arch @julie_netops can you join? I'll ask them to provide their proposed outbound IPs (if they have them) and full VPC CIDR list pre-call.

omar_arch: I can make 9am PT.

julie_netops: ok for 9am PT.

leo_ae: thanks all — I'll paste the firewall snippet into the questionnaire and follow up with finance for a quote. :thumbsup:
